Comparison of the Response with Simulated Responses

Source: R/plot_diagnostic.R
plot_ppc.Rd

Selects the graph that compares the observed response with responses simulated from the fitted distribution. Without statistic, a continuous family gives the observed density with the densities of the simulated responses, and a discrete family the observed counts of each value with the mean and the 90 percent range of the simulated counts. With a function statistic, the graph is the histogram of its value on the simulated responses with the observed value as a line.

Usage

plot_ppc(statistic = NULL, n_sim = 200, seed = NULL, legend = TRUE)

Arguments

statistic

NULL, or a function of a numeric vector that returns a number.

n_sim

The number of simulated responses.

seed

A single number that seeds the simulation, or NULL.

legend

Whether to draw the legend that names the elements of the graph.

Value

A PlotPpc object, inheriting from diagnostic_plot.

Details

The responses are drawn by simulate.StatmodFit() at the fitted parameters, n_sim of them, so they carry the variation of the response and not the uncertainty of the estimates. The densities are computed with stats::density() on a common grid over the range of the observed response. The statistic is a function of a numeric vector that returns one number, such as max or function(y) mean(y == 0). The graph is not defined for a multivariate family.

See also

simulate.StatmodFit(), plot_qq(), diagnostics()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(120))
dd$y <- rpois(120, exp(1 + dd$x))
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::poisson_distrib(), dd)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, plot_type = plot_ppc(n_sim = 50, seed = 1))

ggplot2::autoplot(fit, plot_type = plot_ppc(statistic = max, n_sim = 50,
                                       seed = 1))
